solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sailor taken in merchant vessel that gets shaken

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

indicators.note: taken in by the ear, i.e. heard, so the word for merchant is given by how it sounds

parts.note: a merchant is a seller of goods

explanation.surface: A seaman is taken aboard a trading ship that pitches about in heavy seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' means heard, taken in by the ear. 'vessel' suggests a ship but is a table container.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt cellar is the small container a diner shakes over food to season it.

clue.text: Replace exhaust with parts

indicators.note: parts means splits open, so the word for exhaust is divided by the letter

parts.note: to sap is to exhaust or drain

explanation.surface: A mechanic replaces a car exhaust using spare parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap one thing for another is to exchange or substitute it.

clue.text: Veg on gas uncovered

parts.note: on and leg both name the same side of a cricket field

indicators.note: uncovered removes the top, here the opening letter of the gas word

parts.note: fumes are gas

explanation.surface: Vegetables are cooked on an uncovered gas ring.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Legumes are peas, beans and lentils, vegetables grown in pods.

clue.text: Staff eating desire protective equipment, tucking into a chilli

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the stick word swallows the longing

parts.note: a cane is a staff or stick
a yen is a longing

indicators.note: tucking into means slotting inside the word for a

parts.note: per means a, as in 'ten pounds a head'
PPE is personal protective equipment

explanation.surface: Staff wolfing down food in protective gear tuck into a hot chilli.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' and 'tucking into' are both insertion signals; 'a' meaning per, as in so much a head, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne pepper is a hot red powder made from dried chillies.

clue.text: Restrictive of lithium, metal used in aircraft

parts.note: Li is the chemical symbol for lithium

indicators.note: used in means the metal goes inside the aircraft

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Use of lithium and other metals in aircraft is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something limiting imposes restrictions or constraints.

clue.text: Tree rising in sacred land

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, says the concealed letters are read upwards, so backwards
in says the tree sits concealed within the words sacred land

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tree grows tall on holy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the concealment and 'rising' the upward reading, natural in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a birch-family tree that grows near water.

clue.text: Turners to turn and turn

indicators.note: to turn asks for the word for turners to be flipped and read backwards

parts.note: spinning tops are things that turn

explanation.surface: Woodturners are told to keep turning and turning their work.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'turn' is the definition, in its stage sense: a performer's spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn is a short act in a variety show, also called a spot on the bill.

clue.text: Uneasy arachnophobe scratching bonce after adapting ruler

indicators.note: uneasy signals unsettled letters to be rearranged
scratching means striking out the letters of bonce
after adapting means the rest is reshaped once bonce is gone

parts.note: the word as written is the letter pool
bonce is British slang for head; its letters are removed

explanation.surface: A nervous spider-hater scratches their head after adapting to a ruler's court.
explanation.walkthrough: Take B, O, N, C, E from ARACHNOPHOBE and rearrange ARAHPHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharaoh was a king of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Hold back and study wife cutting potato

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into the potato word, so the others go inside

parts.note: tater is slang for potato
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Someone holds off studying while their wife cuts the potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread water is to hold back from progress, merely staying in place.

clue.text: Some boxes grocer emptied up in arms

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the word for some goes around the other piece

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any bread'

indicators.note: emptied means the inside of grocer is removed, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Some customers are furious when a grocer's boxes are found empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like a noun for the grocer's stock, but it is the verb for enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up in arms is an idiom for being furious and protesting loudly.

clue.text: Stopped fighting crackers pack, cutting ends in foil

parts.note: crackers is slang for mad

indicators.note: in places the trimmed pack inside the sword

parts.note: the foil and the epee are both fencing swords

indicators.note: cutting ends means the first and last letters of pack are dropped, keeping its middle

explanation.surface: Pulling Christmas crackers from a pack, trimmed and wrapped in foil, ends a family squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' and 'foil' look festive and kitchen-bound; one is slang for crazy, the other a fencing sword like the epee. 'cutting ends' trims pack, and 'in' places what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Two parties who made peace ended their hostilities and agreed a truce.

clue.text: After gulping in, answer royal with care

indicators.note: gulping means swallowing, so the word for after takes in the other

parts.note: past means after, as in half past
kingly means royal

explanation.surface: A royal gulps a drink before answering with great care.
explanation.definitionFit: Painstakingly means with meticulous attention to every detail.

clue.text: Screen one Zulu bitten by fat reptile

parts.note: a monitor is a computer screen

indicators.note: bitten by puts the pair of letters inside the word for fat, as if in its jaws

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
I is the Roman numeral one
Zulu is the NATO alphabet word for Z

explanation.surface: A screen shows a Zulu warrior being bitten by a fat reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitten by' means held in the jaws of, so the fat word goes around the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The monitor lizard is a large Old World lizard, such as the Komodo dragon.

clue.text: Beloved entourage's difficult, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the pair of words is wanted for its sound

parts.note: an entourage is a suite, and tough means difficult: suite's tough

explanation.surface: The darling's retinue is proving hard to manage, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: SUITE'S TOUGH said aloud becomes SWEETS TUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet stuff is an old endearment for a darling or loved one.

clue.text: Run around with flyers for films

indicators.note: around asks for the stitching word to be turned back to front

parts.note: to run up a garment is to sew it quickly
terns are seabirds, so flyers

explanation.surface: Someone runs around holding leaflets advertising films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is the dressmaker's sense, to run up a garment; 'around' turns that word, and 'flyers' are birds, not leaflets.
explanation.definitionFit: Westerns are cowboy movies set on the American frontier.

clue.text: Good person, monarch in support group for condition

indicators.note: in places the saint and monarch inside the support group's letters

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is a support group
ST, saint, is a good person
HM is short for His or Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A kindly soul and a king attend a support group about their illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a chronic respiratory illness that narrows the airways.

clue.text: Left section to fill in document

indicators.note: to fill in means the section is put inside the document, filling it

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
a part is a section

explanation.surface: A clerk leaves a section of a form to complete later.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed means went away, i.e. left.

clue.text: Developed new material with European brought to fore

indicators.note: brought to fore means the E is lifted out of its place and put at the very front

parts.note: suede is a soft leather material

explanation.surface: A new fabric was developed and a European firm brought it to market first.
explanation.walkthrough: NSUEDE has its last E, the European, moved to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensued means followed on as a result, so happened or came about.

clue.text: Coming north, salesman with fish in carriage

indicators.note: coming north in a down clue means reading upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
eels are fish

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman heading north carries fish in a railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: REPEELS read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is a railway carriage fitted with berths for overnight travel.

clue.text: One held Munro to be windy — crackpot mountaineered ignoring that

indicators.note: crackpot means crazy, so the letters of mountaineered are scrambled
windy here means twisting, so Munro's letters may come in any order
ignoring that tells us to leave out the letters of the windy Munro

parts.note: the word as written supplies the letter pool
the word as written gives the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A climber finds a Scottish peak too windy and calls the crackpot who climbed it.
explanation.walkthrough: A Munro is a Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet. Remove M, U, N, R, O from MOUNTAINEERED and rearrange TAINEEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A detainee is a person kept in custody, held by the authorities.

clue.text: Bugs tormented fledgelings having escaped shed

indicators.note: tormented means twisted about, so the letters of fledgelings are rearranged
having, with shed, tells us the escaped word is cast off
shed means thrown off, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the word as written is the letter pool
fled means escaped

explanation.surface: Insects pester young birds that have escaped from a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a building but is the removal: FLED out of FLEDGELINGS leaves GELINGS, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Niggles are small worries that bug or irritate someone.

clue.text: That woman records trial, action involving fleecer

parts.note: she is that woman
EPs are extended-play records
a hearing is a trial in court

explanation.surface: A woman records a court trial in which a fraudster is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleecer' suggests a swindler but means one who takes fleeces off sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearing is the removal of wool from sheep, the work of a shearer who takes the fleece.

clue.text: Dropping every case, the fool that makes fuss

indicators.note: dropping every case means stripping each word of its outer letters, its casing

explanation.surface: Someone drops every packing case, and the clumsy fool makes a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a commotion or excited row over something.

clue.text: Fine giving us washing if in bag

indicators.note: if in tells us the answer sits inside the bag word, so taking that word away leaves it

parts.note: we would be bathing when washing ourselves
the word as written, whose letters wrap round the answer

explanation.surface: A fine for us for doing our washing in a bag seems odd.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: the answer, if put in BAG, gives BATHING; so it is BATHING with B, A, G taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine means slender or delicate, as fine thread is thin.

clue.text: First university do held in station

indicators.note: held in puts the hairdo inside the word for station

parts.note: a post is a station, as a sentry's
a do is a hairdo, and a perm is one

explanation.surface: The first university party is held at a railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppermost means highest or foremost, coming first in priority.

clue.text: Bear around church in Alaskan valley

indicators.note: around turns the carrying word back to front

parts.note: to lug is to carry, or bear, something heavy

explanation.surface: A grizzly prowls around a chapel in an Alaskan ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, apt in Alaska, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulch is a narrow steep-sided ravine, a word used in the American West.

clue.text: Passenger just picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for just is wanted for its sound

parts.note: just means fair, as a just ruling

explanation.surface: A taxi passenger was only just picked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A fare is a paying passenger in a taxi or cab.

clue.text: Saw assistant prying around behind earl's back

indicators.note: behind places the assistant and prying words after that letter
back here picks the final letter of earl

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

indicators.note: around flips the word for prying

parts.note: nosey means prying

explanation.surface: An assistant snoops behind a nobleman's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' takes only the last letter of earl, and 'behind' puts the rest after it; 'around' turns the prying word.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay eyes on something is an idiom for seeing it.
